text:
maria (support): FYI escalated from ACME — they report ~15%% of requests failing with 401 signature errors only when routed through our edge gateway. Direct hits to the dedicated endpoint succeed.

maria (support): Attached minimal repro they provided (headers redacted). Problem started after their IdP rotated keys yesterday.

maria (support): logs snippet from edge: 
```
[edge] 2026-03-16T22:10:11Z INFO req_id=abc123 received request x-api-key=redacted
[edge] 2026-03-16T22:10:11Z WARN req_id=abc123 jwt: signature verification failed (kid=7f3b...)
[edge] 2026-03-16T22:10:11Z INFO req_id=abc123 falling back to local cached JWKS (age=423s)
[edge] 2026-03-16T22:10:11Z ERROR req_id=abc123 auth: returning 401
```

maria (support): When they send the same HTTP through curl directly to our origin (bypass gateway) it passes.

sam (eng-security): Interesting — suggests gateway JWKS cache might be stale or there is a key-propagation race. Do we have logs for outgoing JWKS fetches around that time?

dan (sre): I pulled gateway logs — we saw a 200 on JWKS fetch at 22:09:05 and then again 22:11:20. The failing request was at 22:10:11, so there was a newer key available from IdP but gateway still used previous cache. Looks like cache TTL is 60s but fetch jitter + concurrent requests can cause a window.

dan (sre): Also noticed the IdP served Cache-Control: max-age=0 and ETag. Gateway does a conditional GET, but if conditional GET returns 200 with new body at ~22:11 we might have had a race where a request validated against a kid that wasn't in the cached set yet.

sam (eng-security): Two slightly different failure modes here: (1) kid not found in cached JWKS -> should trigger immediate refetch and revalidate, (2) kid present but signature lib returns mismatch if key material rotated with same kid (rare). What error exactly does the jwt library emit? Is it "kid not found" vs "signature mismatch"?

maria (support): Edge log says "signature verification failed (kid=7f3b...)" not "kid not found". ACME sent the token header showing kid=7f3b... and JWKS at the IdP shows that kid existed but rotated to an ephemeral key at 22:09:50.

kevin (oncall): Could be clock skew as well — if IdP issues a new key and signs with a key whose public component hasn't fully propagated to all JWKS endpoints (CDN propagation), signature may fail. Also our edge nodes' JWKS caches are per-node. Traffic routed randomly could hit nodes with different cache states.

olivia (infra-bot): env:gw-jwks-ttl=60s, gw-jwks-stale-allow=5s, jwks-conditional-fetch=true, parallel-verify=enabled

sam (eng-security): Repro steps request: can ACME (or support) capture the raw JWT + the exact JWKS JSON served at same time? We need: token header, token sig, jwks payload, and the edge node id that rejected it. If we can reproduce locally by serving the token while toggling the JWKS set we'll be in good shape.

maria (support): They supplied token header and JWKS payload around 22:10:11, attaching below (redacted). They also note that retries sometimes pass after 1-2s.

maria (support): Quick repro they provided: 1) fetch token from IdP 2) send to our edge via our customer gateway 3) ~1 in 6 responses -> 401.

dan (sre): Hypothesis: edge validation path uses cached JWKS without immediate refetch on signature failure (only on kid-not-found). So signature mismatch won't trigger refetch, causing transient 401 until cache update. That's an unsafe shortcut.

sam (eng-security): Agreed. Fix options: 
- On signature failure, if token.kid present and not revoked, perform a synchronous fetch of the JWKS (conditional GET) and retry verification once.
- Make per-node cache update atomic and publish a short notify to other nodes on successful update (fast invalidation).
- Increase TTL temporarily and rely on ETag/If-Modified-Since to get quick updates (but that doesn't avoid the race).

dan (sre): Quick mitigation we can flip now: enable signature-failure-triggered-refetch = true on gateway cluster and roll a canary to 5%%. That should reduce customer impact without huge perf hit.

maria (support): I'll ask ACME to test canary URL (we have routing to canary 5%%) and report back.

kevin (oncall): Also suggest we log whether refetch was triggered due to "kid-not-found" vs "signature-mismatch" for future triage. Add metric auth.refetch_on_bad_sig.count.

sam (eng-security): Good call. Long-term: consider verifying signatures against both current and previous key sets and implement short overlap window for rotated keys (accept keys with rotation_ts within X seconds), and surface to customers guidance to rotate with key publish-before-sign pattern.

maria (support): ACME confirms after 10m on canary they saw failures drop to ~1/200. They still saw one instance, forwarded logs.

dan (sre): That single instance looks like CDN-edge mismatch at IdP side — the JWKS payload they had showed older key set on one CDN node while another node had new key. We should also add a backoff + retry for conditional GETs that return 5xx from JWKS origin.

sam (eng-security): Action items: 
- dan: enable refetch-on-bad-sig canary (in progress) and add metric (3h)
- olivia: instrument per-node JWKS age and publish cluster invalidation event (48h)
- maria: collect final ACME logs and confirm remediation (support follow-up)
- sam: draft short KB entry for customers about safe rotation (24h)

maria (support): Thanks — I'll update ticket and ask ACME for final verification tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kevin (oncall): If anyone needs to reproduce locally I can spin up a small idp mock that rotates keys mid-run. Ping me and I'll share scripts.

sam (eng-security): Perfect. We'll track this as S-523 in the infra backlog for the more robust fix.

maria (support): Closing loop — ACME verified after 24h no further 401s once canary was expanded and IdP CDN healed. Will file postmortem with root cause (JWKS propagation race + no refetch on bad signature) and mitigation timeline.

maria (support): Postmortem draft will link to this thread and include suggested customer guidance and code snippets for resilient token validation.

acme-ops-bot: Automated note: customer ACME ticket #4521 marked resolved by support."
